title: Check yourself: Integration with Payment Gateways

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A switch maps 1987 terminals, a REST API and a 1993 network link into one internal record, and sends to an acquirer and to one REST gateway. A second REST gateway is added; its API wants every amount as a whole number of minor units. Where does the new work go?

options.text: One new mapping, out of the internal record, since the record already holds each amount with its currency
options.says: with an internal format each endpoint has one mapping; the new destination maps out of the record, and the sources are untouched

options.text: Three new mappings, one from each source, since each source writes its amounts in a different form
options.says: that is the pair-by-pair approach the internal format replaces; the sources' forms were already resolved when they mapped into the record

options.text: A change to every inbound mapping, since the record must hold amounts the way each destination wants them
options.says: the record holds full values, a decimal amount and its currency; each destination converts on its way out

options.text: A change to the packager configuration, since converting an amount is a matter of how field 4 is packed
options.says: packagers and channels only move bytes; the new gateway speaks REST, and the work is in its mapping

origin.section: 12.1. Each Endpoint Maps Into One Internal Format and Out of It

questions.stem: A REST gateway answers a charge with a status that the switch's table of statuses has no entry for. The terminal that sent the 0200 is waiting for field 39. What should the switch do?

options.text: Answer 00, since the gateway answered and only a failed call leaves the charge in doubt
options.says: a status the table lacks may be anything, an approval or not; it is never guessed as an approval

options.text: Answer 05, since a status that is not in the table counts as a decline
options.says: the status may have been an approval, and a decline needs no cancellation, so the money stays taken while the terminal says declined

options.text: Answer 96 and cancel the charge at the gateway, since the status may stand for an approval
options.says: a status the table lacks gets 96, and the payment is cancelled at the gateway, since it may have been an approval

options.text: Answer 96 and leave the charge as it is, since a terminal that gets an error does not complete the sale
options.says: if the status was an approval the card stays charged for a sale that never completed; the charge must be cancelled

origin.section: 12.4. A Value With No Entry in the Table Is Refused, Never Guessed

questions.stem: Your switch forwards a terminal's 0200 to a third-party REST gateway as POST /charges with an Idempotency-Key header. After 15 seconds the call has not returned, and the terminal is still waiting. What should the switch do next?

options.text: Repeat the POST with the same key, since the gateway answers it with whatever came of the first call
options.says: after a timeout the REST client repeats the call with the same key, and the stored outcome tells it what happened

options.text: Repeat the POST with a new key, since the first key belongs to a call that never completed
options.says: a new key is a new payment; if the first call was charged, the cardholder pays twice

options.text: Send the terminal a decline, since a charge whose call timed out was never taken from the card
options.says: a timeout says nothing about the outcome; the gateway may have charged the card

options.text: Send the gateway a refund for the amount, since a refund cancels the charge if there was one
options.says: a refund is a new transaction that credits the card even when nothing was charged; the stored outcome under the key says what happened

origin.section: 12.5. A Retried Call Carries the Same Idempotency Key, So It Is Applied Once

questions.stem: A shop's POST /payments with key k-77 was answered "failed": the acquirer's host never answered, and the gateway reversed the purchase. The cardholder is still at the checkout and wants to try again. What should the shop send?

options.text: The same body with a new key, since k-77 will keep answering with the stored failure
options.says: a retry with the key gets the stored failure; to try again, the shop sends a new payment with a new key

options.text: The same body with key k-77, since the gateway sends a new 0200 for a key whose call failed
options.says: the gateway stores the failure under the key and answers every later call with it; it sends one 0200 per key

options.text: Nothing yet, since the gateway resends the purchase by itself once the host is back
options.says: the gateway never resends an 0200; it reversed this one

options.text: Nothing yet, since a late approval from the host will turn the stored failure into an approval
options.says: the gateway reversed the purchase and stored the failure; that is the outcome every call with the key gets

origin.section: 12.5. A Retried Call Carries the Same Idempotency Key, So It Is Applied Once

concepts: Each endpoint maps into one internal format of full values and out of it, so a new endpoint adds one mapping and each decision about amounts, dates and codes is taken once.
As a REST client, the switch repeats a timed-out call with the same key to learn its outcome, and a new attempt after a stored failure needs a new key.
A gateway status the reply table lacks gets 96 and a cancellation at the gateway, since it may have been an approval.
